extracted_by: hand, T-0290 — the Democrat read, August 1834
note: Vol. I No. 36, the first issue of the month. The local matter is concentrated on page 3: the county's returns from the general election of 4 August, a Marine List that is this pass's first week of the port, a town meeting called by an anonymous elector, one marriage, and the standing advertisements. THE PAGE-4 ADVERTISING IS THE WORST-SEGMENTED IN THE MONTH — six columns cut through the middle of every advertisement, so most of page 4 is not readable to the standard a claim needs and is left unread rather than guessed at. The List of Letters on that page is read anyway, because identifying WHOSE post office it is (Hennepin's, not Chicago's) was a question the ticket put.

[The segmenter has shuffled the two sub-headings ARRIVED and CLEARED and the vessel lines beneath them; the vessels, masters and ports are read as printed and the ARRIVED/CLEARED split is [uncertain: read from the two date runs, 31 July-4 August and 30 July-4 August].]
claims.notes: THE PORT'S OWN WEEK, and the first Marine List this reading pass has taken out of the 1834 Democrat. Seven vessels, all of them schooners or sloops small enough for a river with a bar across its mouth: Lucinda (Hugunin), Austerlitz (M'Kinstry), Bridget (Lundy), Romp (Chaver), Huron (Eno), Phillips (Howe) and Dart (Barnard). The ports they run to are the whole of the town's trade in one week — St. Joseph four times, Detroit twice, Buffalo, New York, Cleveland and Milwaukee once each. St. Joseph is the dominant partner, which is what the Chicago and St. Joseph packet advertisement in this same issue (c007) is selling. NO STEAMBOAT appears in this week's list, which matters for a reconstruction that has to decide what lies at the wharves on a July day: a sloop and a schooner are what the 1834 river carries. The column's headings are transposed by the segmenter, so the ARRIVED/CLEARED assignment per vessel is NOT claimed — only the list and its week.

claims.notes: JOHN H. KINZIE SELLS OUT OF A WAREHOUSE AT FORT DEARBORN, which is a placement a reconstruction can use: not a lot number, but a building whose position is fixed by the fort itself. THE END OF THE WAREHOUSE IS READ 'East' ON TWO WITNESSES OF THREE. The same standing advertisement runs on 1834-08-20 as 'the KAst end of his Wast Hot[use]' (page 3, column 4, line 3175) and on 1834-08-13 as 'the rest end of his WAnt HoUsE' (page 3, column 4, line 2888) — 'KAst' and 'EAst' agree, 'rest' is the odd reading, and no page image is available here to settle it, so the supply is bracketed and this note is the record of the disagreement. The goods list is the ordinary frontier general stock and is kept because the trade a storefront carries is what its sign and its street frontage have to look like.

business.name: Hubbard & Co., agents for the Howard Fire Insurance Company

claims.notes: FIRE INSURANCE IS BEING SOLD IN CHICAGO IN 1834, by Hubbard & Co. as agents for a New York company. Two things follow for the reconstruction and neither is about insurance: a town whose buildings are worth underwriting is a town of built property rather than a post, and a firm that can be appointed a New York company's agent is a firm with a counting-room. The advertisement gives no address, so the placement is `none` rather than a guess; Hubbard & Co. appear elsewhere in this month as references for a tailor (1834-08-06, page 3, column 5) and as sellers of wines, cigars, flour, salt and nails.

claims.notes: THE COUNTY VOTES, 4 AUGUST 1834, AND THE OFFICERS IT NAMES. Cook County has FOUR PRECINCTS at this date, which is the fact of record here: the Democrat can give the returns of 'the four precincts embraced in this county'. The candidate names are the reason to keep it — Silas W. Sherman for sheriff (whose own card to the electors ran on 1834-07-30), and for county commissioner Hunter, James Kinzie, Scarrett and Salsbury, several of whom carry Chicago addresses elsewhere in this corpus. THE NUMBERS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT READ. The table's ruling is gone and the surviving figures cannot be tied to the rows above them without inventing the alignment; a wrong vote total attached to a real name would be worse than none. The canal test the paper describes — both legislative candidates run on their views on the Illinois and Michigan Canal rather than on party — is the local politics of the reconstruction's own subject matter.

Every name is marked [uncertain] by the transcription's own spelling.]
claims.notes: THE MONTH'S ONLY LIST OF LETTERS IS HENNEPIN'S, NOT CHICAGO'S — and that is the finding this claim exists to record, because the ticket asked for the survey to be confirmed while reading rather than trusted. A heading DOES appear in August 1834, here on page 4; the survey that reported none in these four issues missed it. It is the SAME LIST already read at 1834-07-30 (claim c007 there): the Hennepin, Illinois post office, 1 July 1834, signed 'THoS. GALAHER, Jr. P.M.' — whose signature survives in this issue as 'ER, Jr. P.M.' at line 3602, in the second half of the same cut list (claim c010). A three-week standing insertion, in other words, and not a new list. RULING 1 IS THEREFORE NOT ENGAGED: a name on Hennepin's list is not a Chicago resident candidate, so no person is minted from it here. The names are recorded in the quote so the identification can be checked, and 'Gaylord Hayes' is flagged: a 'Gaylard Hayes' appraises the estray in the notice of 1834-07-30, and the coincidence is noted rather than resolved — his alphabetical position between Bar[n]s and Kno[x] is what places him in the list.

Two independent joins on one signature and two names is what carries the identification, and it is what lets this issue's heading be reported as a repeat rather than as a new Chicago list.
